chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all of them, from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him about the divorce of a pregnant woman, so he said: 'One [divorce], and her waiting period is until she gives birth to her pregnancy.'

key_terms.تَضَعَ حَمْلَهَا: She gives birth to her pregnancy

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (iddah) for a pregnant woman after divorce according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam, transmitted through the chain of Sama'ah, clarifies the specific iddah for a pregnant woman, establishing that her waiting period concludes upon childbirth rather than the standard lunar months. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is derived directly from the Quranic verse 65:4, which explicitly links the end of the waiting period to the delivery of the child, distinguishing it from the rulings for non-pregnant women. This hadith serves as a primary textual evidence (hujjah) for the practical application of marital dissolution laws in cases of pregnancy.
